payload.evaluation_method: scratch ESLint 10 flat config with @typescript-eslint/parser under /tmp/gh-aw/eslint-rules, rule implemented as CommonJS matching execa/execa.sync('chmod', [...]) with a -R/-r/--recursive array arg; run against real target sources at commit 42cf8f65ee3a3cc6387cd23c2ac20dcc84f458b0 (src/artifact-preservation.ts, src/container-stop.ts, then full src/**/*.ts excluding *.test.ts)

classifications.detail: execa.sync('chmod',['-R','a+rX',auditDir]) widens permissions on auditDir, which config-writer.ts populates via writeAuditArtifact() using fs.openSync(...,0o600)+fchmodSync(0o600) for squid.conf, docker-compose.redacted.yml, image-manifest.json, policy-manifest.json — matches the rule's unsafe pattern exactly
same auditDestination (default audit dir moved to os.tmpdir()) holds the same 0o600 writeAuditArtifact() files before this recursive chmod runs

chmodRuntimeArtifacts('recursive') default branch invoked for the sessionState (agent-session-state) directory, which only ever holds Copilot CLI events.jsonl/session data written at default (non-restrictive) mode; no 0o600 file writer found for this directory

chmodPreservedDir branch for the moved squid-logs destination dir; squid log files are owned by UID 13 and written at default mode, not 0o600, and are not co-located with the 0o600 api-proxy token-tracker-audit.jsonl (that lives in a sibling api-proxy-logs dir excluded via chmodRuntimeDir:false)

chmod on auditDiagnosticsDir (auditDir/diagnostics), populated only by diagnostic-collector.ts writeFileSync calls at default mode; the sibling 0o600 audit artifacts live in the parent auditDir and are not under this subdirectory
chmod on diagnosticsDestination (os.tmpdir() diagnostics copy) when no auditDir configured; contains only diagnostic-collector.ts default-mode files, no 0o600 content

fixArtifactPermissionsForRootless() runs 'chown -R ... ; chmod -R a+rwX /fix' as a docker exec shell -c string (not an execa('chmod', [...]) array-arg call) against [auditDir, sessionStateDir] — auditDir holds the same 0o600 writeAuditArtifact() files as the true-positive findings above, but the rule's AST match only recognizes the direct execa chmod array-argument form and misses this shell-string form entirely

regression_case.description: src/artifact-preservation.ts preserveCleanupArtifacts(): the auditDir branch (permalink below) must keep failing this rule — it recursively chmods a directory populated by config-writer.ts's writeAuditArtifact(), which deliberately opens each file at 0o600 via fs.openSync+fchmodSync before writing redacted squid.conf/docker-compose/image-manifest/policy-manifest content.

payload.reason: Confirmed false positives on real repository code (sessionState, squid-preserved-dir, and both diagnostics-dir call sites) violate the precision-before-coverage bar even though 2 of 6 flagged sites are true positives; the rule also has a confirmed false negative (artifact-permissions.ts's docker-exec shell-string chmod -R on the same auditDir) and no way to suppress/allowlist directories that are provably free of restricted-mode files, so it is not ready for adoption in this repository without narrowing to directories that provably intersect known-0o600 writers and adding shell-string chmod -R detection plus a suppression mechanism.
payload.smallest_fix: Scope the AST match to only fire when the recursive chmod's target directory argument is a variable that (a) is also passed, in the same file or an imported helper, to an fs.openSync/writeFileSync/chmodSync call with an explicit 0o600 (or narrower) mode, or (b) is annotated via an opt-in JSDoc/comment marker; additionally add a second matcher for execa('docker',['exec'|'run',...]) and execa.sync('sh',['-c', <string containing chmod -R or find -exec chmod>]) calls to catch the artifact-permissions.ts / container-stop.ts shell-string idiom.
